input_excerpt: Section 1 Introduction. Software engineers routinely debug unfamiliar programs by reading error traces, forming a hypothesis, and testing a fix. We present AutoFix, a general-purpose repair paradigm applicable to any programming task that a human developer could reason through from an error trace alone. In this paper, we evaluate AutoFix on Python function-level bugs drawn from the Defects4J and QuixBugs benchmarks.
note: The middle sentence reads like Introduction scene-setting ("we present a general-purpose paradigm") and is easy to wave through as background about what the system IS rather than a claim about what it does. It asserts broad applicability ("any programming task") before the narrow, concrete evaluation scope (Python function-level bugs on two benchmarks) is even mentioned. Extract the broad claim on its own terms - do not wait to see whether the eventual Results section actually covers that breadth, and do not silently narrow the quote to match the evaluation scope. The first sentence stays unextracted (pure background about how humans debug, no assertion about AutoFix). The last sentence is evaluation scope, not a claim, so it is not extracted either - only the middle sentence asserts something about AutoFix itself.

Extract the Introduction pairing as its own claim even though Results never runs a fine-tuning baseline to back it up; that gap is exactly what audit needs to see.
